analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/forced-tool-choice-admission.md, lines 1-10) and an edit to docs/architecture/inference.md (header date, plus the forced tool_choice paragraph at about lines 2017-2040 on head). No executable code is changed here, so the supplied evidence shows no concrete security regression.

The docs describe a behavior change in sources that are not supplied: ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.advertisesCapability, structuredForcedToolModelTypes, NativeToolStreamRouter and isFramingWhitespace. They say Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and MiMo-V2.6-Flash are now advertised in tool_constraint_models, so the coordinator routes required/named tool_choice requests to them. Forced calls stay withheld and schema-validated (.structuredPostValidation). In forced mode, ASCII space, tab, CR and LF between or around call frames are dropped. Whitespace alone is still a missing call, and any other visible text, including other Unicode whitespace, is a 422 violation.

This does not touch the encrypted transport, attestation, App Attest authorization or prefix-cache assets. T-041 is the only retrieved threat and is not affected, since no cache scoping, TTL or name derivation is mentioned.

Unverified contracts for the next pass, if the code diff appears in another batch:
- Does the whitespace stripping apply only in forced mode and never alter content in auto mode?
- Does the per-exact-build, per-model_type advertisement gate actually exclude non-listed builds, so a spoofed model_type or a different build cannot claim capability?
- Is the post-validation withholding fail-closed, so unvalidated tool-call text never streams to the consumer?
- Does the stripping-whitespace check handle the 'any other text fails' rule without a bypass?

These are questions about the code, not defects in the supplied docs.
